spec.title: Example 109 revisited: Hex#toDigit's regression proof with the Character.digit model
spec.description: Example 109 (apache/commons-codec commit 43a9aa66, Hex.toDigit restricted to ASCII) could not make the regression proof between the old toDigit (Character.digit(ch, 16)) and the new one, because JBMC had no usable Character.digit: a stub, or the JDK's own tables read wrongly. jvmcontract now ships a Character model generated from the JDK's decimal-digit table and runs JBMC without its string solver. This job clones the two commits, compiles src/main/java of each with javac, and runs: (1) prove on the OLD version that toDigit(0x0660, 0) == 0, which the earlier run answered wrongly as violated; (2) equivalence between the versions, expected to find the intended change (a Unicode digit the old version decodes and the new one rejects); (3) equivalence with --unchanged-unless 'ch > 127', expected verified: on ASCII nothing changed. A violation in (3) would be a real finding about the commit.
spec.expected: step 3 verified in seconds; step 4 a violation whose witness is a non-ASCII digit, replayed in the interpreter (before: a digit value, after: DecoderException); step 5 verified over every char x int
